original_test_intent: Demonstrate that a correctable ECC fault injected into the primary side of a Full-Mirror GNR memory region is reported by the intended IMC as the expected correctable read error while mirror configuration remains healthy.
original_method: Record DIMM/POR/full-mirror topology and harness limitations; preserve existing memory evidence; verify mirror bit, installed-versus-active half capacity, all-channel mirror state and TAD arrays; use the literal sa2da range to prove address0x100000000 maps to the intended primary MC/DIMM; unlock once, set the exact single-device masks and inject one CE; capture injector plus target IMC/manual MCA decoder MSCOD0x80, ignoring the known incorrect logged address for identity; go, collect platform logs/health and restore settings.
manual_activity: Intel-qualified owner/FAE validates mirror/POR topology, primary-side mapping and harness decoder limitation, then controls injection/go/recovery; agent may correlate mapping and MCA evidence.
required_inputs: GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS and every DIMM PN/serial/slot/POR population
CScripts version/hash/license and documented mirror-size/logged-address sightings
Installed/active capacity, mirror bit, mirrored channels/TAD and primary-versus-mirror MC mapping

review_improvement: Restores source mirror topology and MCA decoding, prevents generic logs or the known-bad address field from falsely proving the target and preserves historical error evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: In Full Mirror mode, a system address resolves to primary and mirror resources; a generic CE proves neither side. The sa2da/TAD outputs and half-capacity invariant establish that the selected address belongs to the intended mirrored region and primary MC. Because the source documents an incorrect logged address, target attribution must come from the precomputed map, masks and controller-local MCA with MSCOD0x80. Clearing or reinjecting would destroy attribution.
